subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack enforce an unconditional 30-second completion deadline for every JSON REST operation while multipart uploads remain unbounded?
rationale: The code and proof establish that the implementation works, but source inspection cannot determine whether slow self-hosted ClickClack deployments and indefinite multipart waits match the intended product contract.

options.title: Approve the current boundary
options.body: Confirm that 30 seconds is the supported maximum for JSON operations and that unbounded multipart uploads are an intentional owner-local exception.

options.title: Retune before merge
options.body: Choose separate owner-local completion limits for bounded JSON calls and potentially long multipart uploads, then update focused proof for both paths.

options.title: Pause the timeout change
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until ClickClack server latency and upload-duration expectations are documented well enough to choose safe deadlines.

recommendation.title: Approve the current boundary
recommendation.body: Confirm that 30 seconds is the supported maximum for JSON operations and that unbounded multipart uploads are an intentional owner-local exception.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available owner for ClickClack product and runtime policy across the server and OpenClaw integration.
